College Park Municipal Court

Address

3717 College St, College Park, GA 30337, United States

Google Maps

MG3X+M9 College Park, Georgia, USA

Time

Working Hours:
Monday: 8:00AM–5.00PM
Tuesday: 8:00AM–5.00PM
Wednesday: 8:00AM–5.00PM
Thursday: 8:00AM–5.00PM
Friday: 8:00AM–5.00PM
Saturday: Closed
Sunday: Closed

Dial

404-767-1537

Website

https://www.collegeparkga.com

Judges

Judge George Barron
Judge Todd Ashley
Judge Sheryl Banes

Magistrate 

CASSANDRA KIRK

Chief Prosecutor

Edward J. Spillane III

Clerk of Courts

Ms. Vanessa Wheeler

College Park Municipal Court is a municipal court located in Georgia. The courtroom listens ordinance violations, problems crook warrants, conducts preliminary hearings, and hears misdemeanor instances of shoplifting and marijuana possession. In Fulton Country jurisdiction for College Municipal is available. In this Court legal dispute are solved according to law. They resolves the issues between people that they do not able to resolve on their own.You can keep in touch with College Park Municipal Court any issues related to legal documents, traffic tickets, business license, utility license etc .

College Park Municipal Court Services

The courts have released an iCourt system. It is a virtual court in which citizens participate with their cases.iCourt will help people in making payment, fines or any extra information on City of College court. You can schedule court dates, payment etc. using this virtual system.

For searching using iCourt, Technical requirements should be followed that are given below:

1.     Laptop or Mobile Device with camera and microphone and internet connection

2.     A good Web Browser like Chrome, Safari

The link used for the login in College Park Municipal Court via iCourt is https://web.icourtapp.com/search

see also What Is The Supreme Court

College Park Municipal Court Ticket Payment

 College Park Municipal Court Ticket can be pay using three way that are: 

In- Person

Pay the fees by coming to the court with the required original document in the working hours.

Online

A person can pay online by clicking on the online payment link on the website using debit, credit of MasterCard, Visa etc.

Phone

 Call on 2404873509 during business hours with your ticket number if you want to pay using a phone with a debit/credit card.

College Park Municipal Court Fine

College Park Municipal Court Fine vary with surcharges like for Block Traffic fine is $145, Doing Business without License Fine is $275 etc.

A person can contact to Court Service in working hours for any information regarding fine

Court Service Contact Number: 404-761-3131 x5100 or x5101

see also The Supreme Court Justice Paradox

College Park Municipal Court Case Search

College Park Municipal Court Case Search can be done using iCourt. You can search your case by login in iCourt and then fill in all the information that are required.

FAQ

1. How Do I Pay a Traffic Ticket?

There are three ways to pay a traffic ticket in College Park Municipal Court:

1. Confirmation

2. Fine Pay

3. Close Case

2. Where can I read all of the College Park Code of Ordinance?

All code is available on the city Clerk Office as well you can read it on the internet using www.municode.com link.

3. Do you have budget billing planning?

Yes, College Park Municipal Court had a budget billing planning. For this planning you must have 12 month of constant service at the same address and fees have been paid before the due date.

 4. What happens when Code Enforcement receives a complaint?

They investigates on the issues and complaints receives from people and gives answer to their questions. After the investigation result come the officer went to the offending property and work with the resident to bog down any violation found.

5. I have question about my utility bills. Who do I call?

Contact Customer Service during the business hours 

(404) 669-3759

6. Can Citizen of College Park submit information for public consumption?

Yes, they can submit information for public consumption using email.

7. How do I establish new residential utility service?

A person must visit the court with some personal documents like name, social security number, address etc. At the time of submitting application deposit is required.

The requirements for deposits are:

  1. Residential Service for Gas and Electric 

• $ 75.00 for one bedroom 

• $85.00 for two bedrooms
• $100.00 for three or more bedrooms 

  1. Total Service

• $125.00 for one bedroom
• $175.00 for two bedrooms
• $200.00 for three or more bedrooms 

8. What are hiring procedure for the City of College Park?

After you submit your application for your desired position the Human Resource department screened your application and check if you meet their requirements. Than selected candidate will get an interview call and after interview the best candidate will be selected.

9. What are hiring procedure for the City of College Park?

After you submit your application for your desired position the Human Resource department screened your application and check if you meet their requirements. Than selected candidate will get an interview call and after interview the best candidate will be selected.

10. I received a traffic ticket and I don’t think it is fair. What can I do?

You should come to the court on your appointed date and time written on your citation if you feel receiving traffic ticket is unfair.

item.title: Girard Municipal Court
item.{http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content:
Girard Municipal Court

Address

100 N Market St A, Girard, OH 44420, United States

Google Maps

100 N Market St, Girard, OH 44420, USA

Time

Working Hours:
Monday: 8:00 AM–4.00 PM
Tuesday: 8:00 AM–4.00 PM
Wednesday: 8:00 AM–4.00 PM
Thursday: 8:00 AM–4.00 PM
Friday: 8:00 AM–4.00 PM
Saturday: Closed
Sunday: Closed

Dial

(330) 545-0069
(330) 545-7045

Website

https://girardmunicipalcourt.com/

Judges

Judge Jeffrey D Adler

Magistrate 

Kurt Latelle

Chief Prosecutor

Michael Bloom

Clerk of Courts

Debbie Santisi

Girard Municipal Courts were established in 1964 by State law and are helping the group of people in Girard, Hubbard Twp, and Vienna Twp. The Girard Municipal Court is the city government judicial branch. They provide fairness and justice to people. They will accurately administrate all the affairs before the Municipal Court. Girard Municipal Court will provide a high level of confidence in the public and fairness through accurate public service. All fines collected by clerks are given out per law to the villages and the state of Ohio.

How to do Case Search?

Girard Municipal Courts Case Search can be done in the following ways:

  • Searching using Name
  • Searching using Case Number
  • Searching using Attorney
  • Searching using Ticket/Citation Number
  • Searching using Advanced Attorney

How to do a Court Fine Payment?

Girard Municipal Court payment can be made in three ways:

In-Person

A person can pay a fine by visiting the court during business hours with necessary documents.

Online

The Girard Court introduced e-Payment. You will make an account on e-payment and then pay online.

Pay by Mail

A person can send a certified check to the mailing address of Girard Municipal Court. The mailing address is 100 N. Market Street, Girard, Ohio 44420.

How much a Case Cost?

Girard Municipal Court Case Cost depends upon the type of case; for speed offense, the total cost of 21+mph over the limit is $197; for improper passing, the total cost is $117; for the victim of criminal case, the total cost is $9, etc.

see also Parker County Texas Court Directory

What Services can I get in GIRAD Court?

Girard Municipal Courts Services includes:

  • Service for Traffic Camera Information
  • Service for Public Access
  • Service of eFiling
  • Service of Payment

is there any Probation in Girard court?

Girard Municipal Court Probation Service Department will perform investigation services for misdeed cases. The probation department's purpose is to encourage justice through community supervisors to protect public safety.

How to get Traffic Camera Information in GIRARD?

Girard Municipal Court Traffic Camera Information will produce extraordinary municipal court services. If any person receives a violation notice from a traffic law photo monitor device, that person will first use the Request For Hearing Form that Girard Municipal Court gives. Then after filling out the form, visit the court during business hours and file your appeal. Lastly, follow the way of contesting the Ticket written on the back of the violation.

What are TIPS to Case Filing in GIRARD MUNICIPAL COURT?

Some tips for case filing in Girard Municipal Court:

  • Selection of Suitable filling action
  • one copy is essential, so avoid sending many copies
  • Single payment is allowed by shopping cart for all the transaction
  • In a correct format like 2015 XXX 12345 enter the case number
  • Avoid the mixing of motion. Separate filing is required by every motion.
  • The court will make all payments in an authenticated way.
  • If the filing is rejected, then contact the Clerk's Office

Clerk Office Contact :(330) 545-3177

What are Juror Rules in GIRARD MUNICIPAL COURT?

Jurors must follow some rules if they are working in the Girard municipal court. They should be punctual and must avoid coming late to court. Jurors must not discuss the case or not talk with any other person during the case. For a biased or unbalanced case, the juror must be open-minded, and for being open-minded, they must watch television and read articles that may occur during the trial. If any juror faces a personal problem, the juror must tell the court before the case.

see also Upson County Courthouse

FAQ

Can the Ticket I received be paid, or do I have to go to court?

If you received a ticket on which a Minor Misdemeanor or mm is written, you could pay it without appearing in court; you can pay it online or mail it to the address. If these words are not written on your Ticket, then your appearance in court is mandatory.

How much is my Ticket?

To see the cost of your Ticket, you can visit Waiver Cost Schedule or contact (330) 545-3049.

Must I bring proof of insurance when paying this Ticket or when going to court?

Yes, you must take insurance proof when going to court for the payment of a ticket.

How do I know the payment has been received if I mail the fine in?

You can use the Public Access System online to see if your fine has been received at their address, or you can contact them at (330) 545-3049 to ask about whether they received the fine or not.

How can I access the e-file?

You can access the e-file by logging into your e-file account. Fill in your username and password in the login window. If you don't have an account, you first made an account on the e-file.

How many rules does Girard Municipal Court have?

Girard Municipal Court rules consist of six local rules of practice and procedure.

What is the First Offender Program?

First Offender Program is a substitute for prospecting a person charged with a misdemeanor crime with no previous criminal judgment.

What are the Program Fees and other expenses of the First Offender Program?

A $200 fee is paid for First Offender Program, and the fees must be paid before entering into the program. The Theft E.D program fee is $50, and it must be paid by the class date.

item.title: Brown County Municipal Court
item.{http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content:
Everything You Need to Know About Brown County Municipal Court: Roles, Procedures, and FAQs

The Brown County Municipal Court, established in 1818 in Ripley and later relocated to Georgetown in 1823, plays a pivotal role in the local judiciary system. It serves as a vital institution for managing traffic violations, misdemeanors, civil disputes under a specified value, and other local cases. The court ensures justice, enforces local laws, and offers public legal services to Brown County residents.

Key Functions of the Municipal Court

Brown County Municipal Court handles a variety of cases and responsibilities, including:

  • Traffic Violations: Managing cases related to driving offenses and violations.
  • Misdemeanors: Addressing lower-level criminal offenses.
  • Small Claims: Resolving disputes involving smaller monetary amounts.
  • Domestic Relations: Handling family matters such as divorce and custody cases.
  • Probation Operations: Supervising probationers and ensuring community safety through rehabilitation programs.

The court also provides a Waiver and Bond Schedule, manages the Probation Department, and offers various legal forms to the public.

Structure and Personnel of the Court

The court is staffed by a dedicated team, including:

  • Judge Joseph M. Worley: Presiding over cases with fairness and adherence to the law.
  • Magistrate Jessica Little: Assisting in legal matters and case adjudication.
  • Chief Prosecutor Zac Corbin: Representing the state in legal proceedings.
  • Clerk of Courts Team: Managing administrative tasks and public records.
    • Wendy Wagner
    • Tami Curliss-Waits
    • Susan Taylor
    • Michelle Kirschner
    • Brandi Warner

Procedures and Processes

Filing a Case

To file a case, visit the court during business hours with all necessary documents. Forms for public records and sensitive documents are available on the court’s website.

Attending a Court Appearance

Court appearances follow a structured process:

  1. Arrive on time at the specified location: 770 Mt Orab Pike, Georgetown, OH 45121.
  2. Present your case or respond to charges.
  3. Follow the judge’s instructions regarding outcomes or next steps.

Paying Fines

Fines can be paid through three methods:

  • In-Person: Visit the court during operating hours (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM–4:00 PM).
  • Online: Use the court’s online payment system.
  • Mail: Send a check to the court’s mailing address.

Case Search Options

Case Search

Enter details like the name, case number, date of hearing, or file date on the court’s website to retrieve case information.

Calendar Search

Search by the beginning date and case type to access calendar-based case details.

Accessibility and Community Impact

The court is committed to:

  • ADA Compliance: Ensuring accessibility for individuals with disabilities.
  • Language Services: Offering translation services for non-English speakers.
  • Community Outreach: Promoting legal literacy and public engagement.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I find my court date?

Contact the Clerk’s Office at (937) 378-3100 or use the online case lookup tool.

Can I pay fines online?

Yes, the court accepts online payments through its website.

What is the court’s contact information?

  • Address: 770 Mt Orab Pike, Georgetown, OH 45121
  • Phone: (937) 378-6358
  • Fax: (937) 378-2462

What are the eligibility criteria for a juror?

  • Must be 18 years or older.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen with good English communication skills.
  • Individuals aged 70+ or professionals such as attorneys, police officers, or dentists are ineligible.

What is the probation department’s role?

The Probation Department supervises offenders, enforces compliance, and facilitates rehabilitation programs to ensure community safety.

What are the passport fees?

  • Passport Book (Adult - First Time): $110 for the U.S. Department and $25 for execution fees.
  • Passport Card (Adult - First Time): $30 for the U.S. Department and $25 for execution fees.
  • Optional Services: Expedite processing ($60) and overnight delivery ($18.30).

Additional Resources

Forms Available

The court provides forms for public records requests and sensitive documents, including identification forms.

Waiver/Bond Schedule

The Waiver/Bond Schedule includes:

  • Natural Resources Watercraft and Wildlife Bond Schedule
  • Traffic and Crime Case Payout Schedule

Title Division Services

The Title Division manages:

  • Proof of ownership
  • Title certification and filing fees
  • Vehicle buying and sales tax processing

Conclusion

Brown County Municipal Court is a cornerstone of the local legal system, ensuring justice, accessibility, and community service. For further assistance, visit the court’s website or contact the Clerk’s Office during business hours.
